courses.title: Physics for Scientists and Engineers: Oscillations, Waves, Electric and Magnetic Fields
courses.description: Lecture/demonstration, four hours; discussion, one hour. Enforced requisites: course 1A, Mathematics 31B, 32A. Enforced corequisite: Mathematics 32B. Fluid mechanics, oscillation, mechanical waves, and sound. Electric charge, field and potential, capacitors, and dielectrics. Currents and resistance, direct-current circuits. P/NP or letter grading.
courses.prereqs_raw: Enforced requisites: course 1A, Mathematics 31B, 32A. Enforced corequisite: Mathematics 32B.

courses.title: Physics for Scientists and Engineers: Electrodynamics, Optics, and Special Relativity
courses.description: Lecture/demonstration, four hours; discussion, one hour. Enforced requisites: course 1A, 1B, Mathematics 32A, 32B. Enforced corequisite: Mathematics 33A. Magnetic fields, Ampere’s law, Faraday’s law, inductance, and alternating current circuits. Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, light, geometrical optics, interference and diffraction. Special relativity. P/NP or letter grading.
courses.prereqs_raw: Enforced requisites: course 1A, 1B, Mathematics 32A, 32B. Enforced corequisite: Mathematics 33A.

courses.title: Physics Laboratory for Scientists and Engineers: Mechanics
courses.description: Laboratory, four hours. Enforced requisite: course 1A or 1AH. Enforced corequisite: course 1B or 1BH. Computerized measurements of uniform and accelerated motion, including oscillations. Analysis of data and comparison of results to predictions, including least-squares fitting. Conception, execution, and presentation of creative projects involving motion. Letter grading.
courses.prereqs_raw: Enforced requisite: course 1A or 1AH. Enforced corequisite: course 1B or 1BH.

courses.title: Physics Laboratory for Scientists and Engineers: Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Laboratory, four hours. Enforced requisites: courses 1A or 1AH, 1B or 1BH. Enforced corequisite: course 1C or 1CH. Sound waves and electric circuits, taken by digital oscilloscopes and analyzed by Fourier transformation. Geometrical and physical optics.
